**Finding: COMPLIANT (sits at fallback, in part above it).**

Section 8 carries a genuine Commerce One IP indemnity in our favour:

- **Vendor IP indemnity (fallback element 1):** §8.1 — "indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers" against claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights; it even extends to our Customers and includes an express duty to defend (a preferred-level feature).
- **Customary exclusions (elements 2–4):** §8.2 limits cover for use outside the Documentation and third-party modification — these are permissive allowances, and their narrowness (no combination/specification carve-outs) favours us.
- **Remedy ladder (element 5):** procure the right, replace or modify to make non-infringing, failing which terminate and "refund to Corio a pro-rated portion of the fees paid hereunder" (element 6).
- **Super-cap (element 7):** exceeded — §9 twice carves "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" out of both the 12-month cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, leaving the indemnity uncapped rather than capped at 3× annual fees.
- **Customer indemnity:** searches for "indemn"/"defend" return only §8; there is no Corio-side indemnity to narrow, so no walk-away or one-way risk.

Noted for the rationale only, not redlined: the indemnified item is the defined "Software" rather than also the MarketSite.net Service, and there is no separate indemnity for breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct — preferred-level gaps that do not defeat the fallback. No redline proposed.
